summary.headline: Shadowfax Q2 FY27 revenue rose 57% YoY to INR1,538 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin of 5%, its first time crossing INR1,500 crore and 5%.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR1,538 crore, up 57% YoY and 13% QoQ, despite no festive sales-season revenue in the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was INR77 crore at a 5% margin and PAT was INR67 crore. Operating space expanded from 53 lakh to 69 lakh sq ft ahead of the festive peak, and the delivery partner base grew 31% QoQ. Management kept the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance but declined to revise near-term guidance until Q3 performance is seen. Management also announced a micro-fulfillment centre (MFC) business and disclosed that exposure to the largest customer fell by at least 3-4 percentage points versus its long-term average.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR60 (from around INR55 last quarter)

segments.name: Express Parcel
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,096 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) on 21.7 crore shipments; share of revenue fell to 71% from 73% in Q1. Express realization was broadly flat QoQ and marginally down YoY.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Revenue INR341 crore (+88% YoY, +26% QoQ); share of revenue rose to 22% from 20%. Realization per order rose about 13% QoQ, helped by longer-distance food delivery after aggregators moved to 0% commission.

segments.name: Other logistics services (CriticaLog, Dark Stores, value-added)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR100 crore, up 13% QoQ, as CriticaLog (serving more than 550 customers) and Dark Stores scale. Value-added services are guided at 35%-40% of revenue.

segments.name: Prime Large (bulky)
segments.commentary: Annualized run rate above INR100 crore, up 33% QoQ; white goods and value-added services are in pilot.

segments.name: D2C and SME (Shadowfax 360)
segments.commentary: D2C business more than doubled YoY, with market share above 14% (up 2 pp QoQ). Shadowfax 360 has more than 6,700 sellers ordering within 200 days of launch.

guidance_outlook: Long-term cumulative revenue growth guidance of 27%-30% maintained; near-term guidance not revised until Q3 results are seen.
Express Parcel expected to grow at a 27%-28% CAGR, driven by market growth and share gains.
Quick commerce industry expected to compound at 30%+; Shadowfax assumes it keeps its market-leader share.
Capex guided at 3.8%-4% of revenue for the year, including MFC and Dark Store capex; management said the capex cycle is on track.
Micro-fulfillment centre business to be built over the next 6-12 months; revenue this year expected to be small.
Two mega sorters and volume profilers to go live in Q4 FY27; next lost-shipment feedstock target of 4% expected in a few quarters.
capex_capacity: Total operating space expanded from 53 lakh sq ft to 69 lakh sq ft in Q2, the largest capacity addition in company history.
Middle-mile footprint rose from 24 lakh sq ft to more than 34 lakh sq ft; about 5% of total space is temporary peak-season pop-ups that will wind down.
Dark Stores: 70 opened by end-Q2 FY27 against a target of 100 for the year, across 9 cities; more than 4,000 unique Dark Stores served across quick commerce players.
Planned MFCs of about 40,000-50,000 sq ft; management sees room for MFCs across 50 cities over the next few years.
Delivery partner network grew 31% QoQ, from 2.9 lakh to 3.8 lakh.
demand_pricing: Same-day/next-day Prime delivery is offered across more than 120 cities; management says realization is 15%-20% higher for same-day delivery on the same network.
Customers outside the top 10 are the fastest-growing group; management says the largest customer's share fell by at least 3-4 pp versus its long-term average.
Amazon became a top-5 customer within a year of launch; e-commerce integrations are mostly complete.
Express realization is affected by mix (weight, zones, and Prime's shorter distances), and management expects it to stay in a similar range in the short term.
Management cited a 0% commission model in food delivery as a driver of higher-realization longer-distance orders.

qa_highlights.question: Given the festive season shift to Q3, will guidance be revised upward in the near and medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will wait for Q3 results before revising guidance; the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance is maintained, and it is too early to judge the rest of the sale season.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Hyperlocal realization increase, and how long will it last?
qa_highlights.answer: Realization rose from about INR55 to above INR60, driven by distance and mix: higher on-demand and long-distance orders, plus food delivery growth after the 0% commission model.

qa_highlights.question: What cost build-up hit margins ahead of the season?
qa_highlights.answer: Rental cost rose from 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue (about 30 bps), and depreciation rose slightly. Last-mile and contractual labour scaling had no P&L impact because of the crowdsourced model.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower dependence on the main customer seasonal or strategic?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure fell by at least 3-4 pp from the long-term average this quarter. Management attributes it to strategy (growth in D2C, SME, Prime Large and Hyperlocal), with the enterprise business growing more slowly.

qa_highlights.question: How do MFCs differ from Dark Stores, and is the capex inside the 3.8%-4% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dark Stores deliver in 15-30 minutes; MFCs target 8-12 hour delivery from 40,000-50,000 sq ft sites with 5-10 co-located brands near city-edge sort centres. The capex guidance includes MFCs and Dark Stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Express realizations flat despite more Prime Large and D2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix effects (weight, zones, and shorter-distance Prime orders) offset gains. Realization was marginally up QoQ, marginally down YoY, and is expected to stay in a similar range short term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added services mix and the 2-year outlook for Express versus Hyperlocal?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added services are 35%-40% of revenue and are expected to hold that ratio over 3-5 years. Express and Hyperlocal are not expected to shift materially in mix over the next two years.

risks_watch: Customer concentration: management aspires to bring top-customer exposure significantly below 40%, but has not given a number.
Q3 festive-season performance, which will determine whether guidance is revised.
Rental cost at 3.5% of revenue; management is unsure whether it will fall next quarter.
Partner expense rising with Hyperlocal mix; depreciation rising with capex.
Express realization flat YoY; mix shift toward Prime may keep it under pressure.
MFC business is new and capital-heavy, with small revenue expected this year.
Quick commerce competition, although all players are growing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margin and share gains, but cautious on guidance: management declined to raise it and said it is too early to judge the rest of the festive season. Answers on realization and cost mix were detailed, while the exact customer-concentration figure was withheld.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Same-day Prime delivery in 120+ cities
rows.why: Same-day/next-day Prime is offered across more than 120 cities and realization is 15%-20% higher for same-day delivery on the same network, so the mix shift is likely to keep lifting realization.

rows.label: Customer concentration falling
rows.why: Largest customer's share fell by at least 3-4 pp versus its long-term average, and management aspires to get top-customer exposure well below 40% without giving a number.

rows.label: Lost-shipment feedstock target of 4%
rows.why: Management expects the next lost-shipment feedstock target of 4% in a few quarters, after the two mega sorters go live in Q4 FY27; no current figure given.
